findings.title: Login-list invalidation is skipped for updates made while an organization is disabled
findings.body: `original` is obtained through this provider's `getById`, which wraps organization-linked providers so that `isEnabled()` is false when their organization is disabled. A caller can likewise pass the wrapped model returned by `session.identityProviders().getById()` to `update`. In that case, an update that changes a cached-list-relevant property (for example `hideOnLogin`, `BROKER_PUBLIC`, or the organization ID) while the organization is disabled makes both predicate evaluations false and returns at line 405 without invalidating the login-list keys. The lists themselves were populated from the raw JPA delegate, however, so they still contain IDs based on the static IDP properties. After the organization is enabled, an old organization query can return an IDP now linked to a different organization, or omit an IDP that became login-eligible. Invalidation decisions need to use the raw stored login properties or invalidate on these updates rather than using the organization-aware `isEnabled()` wrapper.

findings.title: The new test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of created providers
findings.body: Each of the twenty providers created in this test is registered for cleanup using `identityProviders().get("alias")`, not its actual `idp-alias-N` value; the additional provider at line 425 has the same problem. Cleanup therefore leaves the providers created by this test in the shared test realm (and may remove an unrelated provider actually named `alias`), allowing later tests or retries to observe polluted data and making their result counts non-deterministic. Register cleanup using the alias created for each representation.
